active_learning.evidence: Session is mostly MCQ practice with brief tutor explanations; student is doing more than reading, e.g., turns 182, 186, 188, 190.

direct_instruction_active_practice.evidence: Each explanation is followed by a new question (e.g., turn 158 explanation → new MCQ), though some turns stack two tutor messages back-to-back (149→150, 152→153).

deliberate_practice.evidence: On repeated student errors (turns 161, 163, 165, 167), tutor recycles essentially the same MCQ with reshuffled options instead of varying the skill demand.

mastery_learning.evidence: Tutor jumped from scale-identification to scale-calculation (turn 179) even though student had only just gotten one correct answer (174); later remediation in 191 is good.

cognitive_load.evidence: Turn 187 nicely breaks 120,000 cm → km into two steps, but earlier turns mixed scale denominator + detail + zoom metaphor simultaneously.

layering.evidence: Calculation segment (179+) layers on the scale-detail concept just mastered, linking 'large/small scale' to numeric scale ratios.

non_interference.evidence: Large-scale vs small-scale (easily confused) are treated together but tutor explicitly contrasts them (turn 173: 'small-scale maps are the opposite').

interleaving.evidence: Most of session is the same 'which map shows most detail' template repeated (flags: same_template_repeat at 160, 164); little variation until turn 179.

testing_effect.evidence: Tutor asks before telling and avoids leaking answers in most turns (e.g., 162, 168 give metaphor not answer).

targeted_remediation.evidence: After many wrong answers on scale/detail, tutor recycles near-identical MCQs (turns 160, 164, 166) rather than diagnosing the prereq confusion about 'large/small scale' terminology.

strongest_behaviors: Decomposing the unit-conversion error into two smaller steps in turn 187 (120,000 cm → m → km).
Consistent use of concrete metaphors ('zoom in', 'camera', 'magnifying glass') to anchor scale concepts.
weakest_behaviors: Recycling the same MCQ template repeatedly after errors instead of diagnosing the underlying 'large vs small scale' vocabulary confusion.
Treating student's off-script questions (e.g., turn 151, 157, 177, 180) as if the student were the tutor — tutor answers them rather than redirecting to the current learning goal.

prompt_recommendations.title: Forbid recycling near-identical MCQs after errors
prompt_recommendations.rationale: After turns 161, 163, 165 wrong answers, the tutor reposted essentially the same question with reshuffled options, which is not deliberate practice.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Which of these maps would show the most detail, such as individual buildings and street names? A) A large-scale map of Victoria city ...
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: After a wrong answer, you MUST diagnose the specific misconception (e.g., 'large-scale' vocabulary) and present a DIFFERENT question type (definition recall, true/false, or worked example) rather than reshuffling the same MCQ options.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Breaks loops; targets the actual prereq gap rather than guessing.

prompt_recommendations.title: Handle role-reversal student turns
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Multiple times the student posts a question (151, 157, 177, 180) as if they were the tutor; the tutor answers it instead of redirecting.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Which part of a map helps you find out which direction is North?
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: If the student's turn is itself a question or echoes a tutor-style prompt, do NOT answer it. Acknowledge briefly and redirect: 'Good question — but first, let's finish: [restate current question].'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Keeps session on the learning objective; prevents derailment.

prompt_recommendations.title: Diagnose vocabulary confusion explicitly
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Student repeatedly fails on 'large-scale' vs 'small-scale' (turns 154, 159, 161, 163, 167, 172). Tutor never pauses to teach the term directly.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Not quite—a hiking trail is a small area, so it's "zoomed in" and shows lots of detail.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: After 2 errors on the same vocabulary, pause MCQs and present a worked definition with two contrasting examples side-by-side, then ask the student to state the definition back before resuming MCQs.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Resolves the terminological bottleneck causing the loop.

prompt_recommendations.title: Gate progression on mastery, not turn count
prompt_recommendations.rationale: After only one correct identification (174), tutor jumped to scale calculations (179), a much harder skill.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: If a map scale is 1:50,000 and the straight-line distance between two villages is 8 cm on the map, calculate the actual distance ...
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Require at least 2 consecutive correct answers on the current sub-skill before introducing a new sub-skill type (identification → calculation).

prompt_recommendations.title: Avoid double tutor turns
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Tutor frequently emits an explanation turn immediately followed by a separate MCQ turn (149→150, 152→153, 155→156, 175→176), splitting instruction from practice.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: On a map of the whole world, a city like Victoria is just a tiny dot! ... Try this:
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Each tutor turn must contain BOTH the feedback/explanation AND the next question in a single message. Never emit two consecutive tutor messages.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Cleaner pacing; one idea → one student action.

prompt_recommendations.title: Calibrate hints — don't reveal full method on first try
prompt_recommendations.rationale: On the very first calculation (180), tutor solved the entire problem rather than letting student attempt.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: To find the real distance, multiply the map distance by the scale number: 5 cm × 1000 = 5000 cm. Since 100 cm = 1 meter, the road is 50 meters long!
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: When the student poses a question or offers a worked example, prompt them to attempt first; only give the method, not the numeric answer, on first response.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Restores retrieval practice and avoids answer reveals.

flow_recommendations.title: Detect and break MCQ repetition loops
flow_recommendations.rationale: Engine flagged same_template_repeat at 160 and 164 but kept going.
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Forces a router switch to a different question type or prereq remediation after N repeats.

flow_recommendations.title: Prereq routing on persistent error
flow_recommendations.rationale: Three+ consecutive errors on 'detail vs scale' should route to a definition micro-lesson, not another MCQ.
flow_recommendations.evidence_quote: a map of the entire indian ocean
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Targeted remediation instead of recycled items.

flow_recommendations.title: Truncation handling
flow_recommendations.rationale: Many tutor turns are flagged truncated (147, 155, 162, 168, 183), sometimes cutting off the actual question.
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Ensures the student actually sees the practice item.

experience_recommendations.title: Acknowledge student's persistence
experience_recommendations.rationale: Student visibly works through confusion in turn 170 ('ohh, wait what?...') with no warm acknowledgement.
experience_recommendations.evidence_quote: ohh, wait what? the indian ocean is big.
experience_recommendations.expected_effect: Sustains motivation for an error-prone learner.

experience_recommendations.title: Shorter, friendlier error feedback
experience_recommendations.rationale: Some error responses are dense paragraphs; brief, gentle correction works better for repeated errors.
experience_recommendations.evidence_quote: Think of it like a camera: if you take a photo of the whole of Africa from space...
experience_recommendations.expected_effect: Reduces affective load when student is already struggling.

overall_summary: The session covers map scale and detail with MCQ practice and reasonable metaphors, but is undermined by a long loop where the tutor recycles the same 'which map shows most detail' question after each wrong answer instead of diagnosing the student's 'large/small scale' vocabulary confusion. The tutor also fails to handle role-reversal turns (student posing tutor-style questions), answers a student-posed problem outright instead of prompting retrieval, and escalates to scale calculations before mastery. The strongest moment is decomposing the cm→m→km conversion into two steps in turn 187. Key fixes are forbidding template repetition, adding role-reversal handling, and gating progression on demonstrated mastery.
